title: Active Data Controllers may reference their own Active Data as logic, letting rules self-modify at high speed
content:
A.1.2.2.2.15 defines the Active Data Controller as a Primary Document that names "the entities who are authorized to modify the child Active Data Documents" and "the authorized process by which said Active Data Documents are modified." It must have an Active Data Directory at .0.6.

The striking clause is in Additional Logic: "The Active Data Controller Document can reference its Active Data subdocuments for its own logic. This allows Active Data Documents to be self-improving and adaptive at high speeds."

That is a deliberate reflexive loop. The Controller is a Primary Document, amendable only through governance cycles; its Active Data children are modifiable in real time. By letting the Controller's rules *point at* its fast-moving children, part of the effective rule becomes real-time state. Parameters, authorized-actor lists, or thresholds can change between governance cycles without any Primary Document being edited.

The power here should not be understated: it means the boundary between rule and data is set by the Controller's author, and a Controller can be written to delegate as much of its own logic as it likes into the fast lane. A.1.2.2.2.17 reinforces the openness — Active Data "can contain arbitrary types of data, including large amounts of data or code."

The containment is that the delegation must be *explicit and pre-declared* in a document that only governance can change. Governance controls the shape and the reach of the loop; it just does not control each turn of it. That is the same bargain as the Active Data carve-out generally, applied one level up.
description: A.1.2.2.2.15 says a Controller 'can reference its Active Data subdocuments for its own logic', which it explicitly frames as allowing Active Data to be self-improving and adaptive.
